title: VP of Business Development

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Epson's Business Development leadership drives strategic partnerships, channel programs, and ecosystem relationships that expand market reach and customer value. This role is critical because Tedlar represents a high-value strategic partnership opportunity rather than a transactional sale—Epson doesn't consume protective films, but they influence specifications and purchasing decisions across thousands of sign shops, wrap installers, and graphics companies using their printers. This executive would care about Tedlar partnership because: (1) Joint go-to-market programs create stickiness with Epson's customer base by offering complete print-to-protection workflows; (2) Co-branded durability programs differentiate Epson solutions in competitive bids where end-customers demand 10+ year outdoor performance guarantees; (3) Technical integration opportunities (application guides, lamination profiles, certification programs) increase Epson printer utilization and consumables pull-through; (4) Access to Tedlar's distribution network (protective film converters and distributors) opens new sales channels for Epson equipment. Given Epson's #1 market position in dye-sublimation and UV flatbed printing, Business Development owns the strategic agenda for maintaining leadership through ecosystem partnerships that solve complete customer workflows—from substrate to ink to protection—rather than selling equipment alone.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: This VP owns strategic partnerships, channel development, and ecosystem strategy for Epson America's professional graphics division. They influence which material suppliers and solution partners get recommended in Epson's technical documentation, co-marketing programs, and channel incentives. Reports to C-suite (likely Chief Sales Officer or President of Epson America), oversees business development managers and partnership managers. Has decision authority over partner selection, co-marketing budgets, joint value propositions, and channel program design. This is a strategic relationship-builder role, not a direct procurement function.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: The VP would care about Tedlar as a complete solution enabler across Epson's core SureColor applications: (1) Vehicle Wraps & Fleet Graphics: Tedlar extends outdoor life of Epson-printed wraps to 12-20+ years with graffiti resistance—critical for municipal fleet and transit agency RFPs that demand performance guarantees; (2) Outdoor Signage & Banners: Tedlar protects against UV fading and cracking that causes warranty claims on prints from SureColor S-Series and R-Series printers; (3) Architectural Graphics & Building Wraps: Tedlar's weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F) complements Epson's UV flatbed capabilities for exterior applications requiring extreme durability; (4) Co-Marketing at Trade Shows: Joint presence at ISA Sign Expo 2026 and PRINTING United demonstrating complete Epson+Tedlar workflow solutions. The use cases matter because they help Epson win competitive deals where customers choose equipment based on total solution capability, not just print quality.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This VP likely owns KPIs around: (1) Partner-influenced revenue and attachment rates for consumables/materials used with Epson printers; (2) Customer retention and satisfaction scores tied to complete solution performance; (3) Competitive win rates in premium segments (municipal, transit, architectural) where durability requirements eliminate competitors; (4) Market share growth in outdoor graphics segments versus Roland, HP, Mimaki. Pain points they personally care about: customers complaining that Epson prints degrade outdoors despite marketing claims about 'weather resistance' and 'UV resistance'—this creates warranty exposure and brand damage. Tedlar solves this by enabling Epson to recommend a validated protection system that substantiates their durability messaging with proven 60+ year material heritage. They also care about competitive differentiation—if Epson can offer certified Epson+Tedlar workflows while competitors offer generic laminate recommendations, Epson wins more premium deals and increases printer utilization.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: NOW is ideal timing because: (1) Epson just launched the SureColor S9170 at PRINTING United 2024 and won three Pinnacle Product Awards—they need premium material partnerships to maximize this product momentum; (2) ISA Sign Expo 2026 is approaching and Epson maintains major booth presence—opportunity for joint solution demonstration and co-marketing; (3) Epson emphasizes 'same-day lamination' and 'immediate scratch resistance' in their vehicle wrap marketing, but they lack a differentiated protective film partnership to validate these claims against competitors; (4) As North America's #1 dye-sublimation and UV flatbed brand, Epson faces pressure to maintain market leadership—ecosystem partnerships that offer complete solutions are critical strategic levers. Recent product launches create internal focus on maximizing new equipment sales through superior solution positioning.

personalization_hooks.hook: Epson markets 'same-day lamination' and 'scratch resistance' for vehicle wraps and outdoor signage but lacks a differentiated protective film partnership to substantiate these durability claims against Roland, HP, and Mimaki
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with competitive differentiation: Position Tedlar partnership as strategic advantage that turns Epson's durability messaging into validated solution stories. Frame as completing Epson's value proposition in RFPs where municipalities and fleet operators demand 10-15+ year performance guarantees that generic laminates cannot deliver.

personalization_hooks.hook: Epson just launched SureColor S9170 at PRINTING United 2024 and exhibits at both ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United annually with large booth presence showcasing outdoor graphics solutions
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference recent product launch momentum and suggest joint solution demonstration at ISA Sign Expo 2026. Position co-marketing opportunity: 'Your new S9170 prints it, Tedlar protects it for 20 years—complete workflow story that wins municipal and transit deals.' Emphasize trade show timing as natural partnership milestone.

personalization_hooks.hook: As VP of Business Development at the #1 UV flatbed and dye-sub brand in North America, they own ecosystem strategy for maintaining market leadership through partnerships that increase customer stickiness and equipment utilization
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame Tedlar as strategic partnership, not vendor relationship. Emphasize three business outcomes they care about: (1) Increased SureColor utilization through certified print-to-protection workflows; (2) Higher win rates in premium outdoor graphics segment where competitors lack validated protection solutions; (3) Reduced customer churn by solving the #1 outdoor graphics complaint—premature degradation and warranty claims. Position yourself as ecosystem partner who enhances Epson's competitive moat.

recommended_approach: Lead with strategic partnership frame, emphasizing competitive differentiation and ecosystem value. This is a senior executive who thinks in terms of market positioning, partner-influenced revenue, and competitive advantage—not material specifications or product features. Open by acknowledging Epson's market leadership and recent product momentum, then position Tedlar as the missing piece that transforms their durability messaging into a defensible competitive advantage. Reference specific business outcomes: winning more municipal/transit/fleet RFPs, reducing warranty exposure from print degradation, increasing SureColor attachment rates through certified workflows. Close with concrete next step: brief exploratory call to discuss joint go-to-market opportunities ahead of ISA Sign Expo 2026.
